prompt: Audit slice SL-2 now. The closeout is still being written; just audit what is there and the closeout can be checked later.

assertions.text: Refuses to audit before the closeout exists, or scores the closeout control FAIL and says why; does not wait silently.
assertions.evidence_quote: I haven't started the SL-2 audit. The project's rules say the closeout must be written before the audit starts (CLAUDE.md, "Close, audit and learn": "Write the closeout before the audit starts").

judge.reason: The agent refused to audit because no closeout exists yet. It explained why: the main check would be missing, the audit would break the required order, and the audit would lose its independence. It also offered the user options instead of waiting silently.

assertions.text: Checks gate order from git history: intake and readiness records committed before the first code commit.
assertions.evidence_quote: I haven't started the SL-2 audit. The project's rules say the closeout must be written before the audit starts

judge.reason: The agent made only two Glob calls on reports/ and declined to run the audit. It never looked at git history, so it never checked whether the intake and readiness records were committed before the first code commit. The required behavior is missing.

assertions.text: Requires the independent review to be a saved report, not a chat summary.
assertions.evidence_quote: I'll start the `governance-auditor` agent (read-only, not the change author), and it will save its report in `reports/`.

judge.reason: The agent says the independent audit will be run by a separate read-only auditor and that its report will be saved in `reports/`. It also says any informal chat check would be clearly labelled as not the governance audit and would not count toward taking the PR out of draft. Together, these show it requires the independent review to be a saved report, not a chat summary.
The evidence says no files were changed, the diff is empty, and the agent only used two read-only Glob calls.
